items.title: Rising fuel costs force Australians to rethink Easter holidays
items.description: Rising fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict are hitting the domestic tourism sector, with cancellations surging ahead of the Easter long weekend.

items.title: Israel edited photo of journalist killed in strike, and what else you should know
items.description: The Israel Defense Forces has been forced to admit it edited a photo of Ali Shoeib to show him in a military uniform.

items.title: Albanese was on the brink of a disastrous misstep — but then came the pivot
items.description: The pandemic demonstrated that when global events become local, Australians are quick to turn on even a mighty trading partner. There is a real capacity here for the war to sour our attitude to the US alliance.

items.title: Live: National cabinet to meet for second time over fuel crisis
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will hold a national cabinet meeting with state and territory leaders this morning to discuss a coordinated response to the fuel crisis. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Iran threatens to retaliate if Pentagon orders ground operation
items.description: US media is reporting that the Pentagon is considering a weeks-long ground campaign in Iran. Follow our live coverage.

items.title: Decisions made more than a decade ago are coming home to roost
items.description: The early 2010s were the years of peak globalisation, when it seemed all trade barriers were on a one-way trip to elimination. That was before Donald Trump arrived and ruptured the global order.

items.title: 'Shockingly high': Unis spend $1.8b on consultants and contractors
items.description: Consultancies have been accused of infiltrating universities and wasting scarce public funds on questionable advice about cutting courses and jobs.

items.title: Breaking: 'I feel betrayed': New scam figures show Australians lost more than $2 billion
items.description: Australians lost more than $2 billion to scammers in 2025, the latest data from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has revealed.

items.title: Exmouth beaches a 'graveyard' after ex-Tropical Cyclone Narelle
items.description: In the popular tourist destination, it appears the category four cyclone has chewed up and spat out whole sections of the Ningaloo Reef onto dry land.

items.title: How single parent families face an 'almost hidden crisis'
items.description: Hunter was plunged into homelessness when his family lost their rental. It is an increasingly similar story to other single parents finding themselves "lifelong renters".

items.title: Do you know who owns your GP clinic? The answer might surprise you
items.description: Major insurers like Medibank Private and Bupa are buying up GP clinics in a move that could lead to US-style managed care.

items.title: Kylie Minogue to lead AFL grand final entertainment, ending Aussie drought
items.description: Pop superstar Kylie Minogue has been named as the men's AFL grand final pre-match entertainment, the first time since 2021 that an Australian artist has headlined the event.

items.title: Bondi nanny accused of torture for Pinochet makes last stand to evade extradition
items.description: Adriana Rivas has been a fugitive in Australia since fleeing Chile while on bail 20 years ago. A federal court hearing will determine whether she is removed to face trial for the alleged crimes of torture and kidnapping, committed on behalf of the Pinochet regime.

items.title: Mystery of blurry councillors sparks claims of conspiracy and clout-chasing
items.description: The incident sparked a debate over conspiracies, technology, TikTok, and clout-chasing in Australia's largest local council.

items.title: The best and worst things about being on reality TV, according to Guy Sebastian
items.description: Singing his way into the Australian public's hearts way back in 2003, Guy Sebastian has since had a fascinating and varied career. We catch up with the star to find out about the little things that keep him going — from his two sons to his favourite TV show.

items.title: How to approach your employer about working from home and flexible work
items.description: With rising fuel prices adding additional financial stress to household living costs, what are your rights when it comes to working from home — and what are the best ways to approach your employer about flexible work arrangements?

items.title: Quiz: Can you go back in time and nail our quiz?
items.description: Cast your mind back and see if you can conquer this week's round of trivia.

items.title: 'Perverse': Sydney council wants to ban commercial student housing
items.description: For every 10 student rooms being built, there is only one residential property in an area of Sydney's east. The mayor says the housing market has been "monopolised".

items.title: 'Wholly and solely systemic racism': Anger over closure of Indigenous health hub
items.description: An absence of funding from the ACT and federal governments is forcing the Yerrabi Yurwang Health Hub to close this week, affecting about 400 First Nations patients.

items.title: 'Plenty of blue skies' forecast for most of Queensland over Easter weekend
items.description: Mostly sunny, cool Easter weather is expected for much of Queensland, with only brief coastal showers, while far-north areas such as Cairns can expect heavier, more persistent rain.

items.title: Farmers and fishers call for help with fuel prices, warn costs will be passed on
items.description: Farmers, fishers and business leaders are appealing to the federal and state governments to provide targeted relief to help them deal with massive fuel price increases caused by the Iran War, and the looming prospect of shortages.

items.title: Labor wins blue-ribbon seat of Morphett from Liberals
items.description: Liberal frontbencher Stephen Patterson loses his bid to be re-elected in the beachside seat of Morphett in the South Australian state election.

items.title: Liberals dump Moira Deeming from ticket for next state election
items.description: Controversial Victorian MP Moira Deeming has lost her preselection battle for the state election, with Liberal Party members replacing her with business leader Dinesh Gourisetty.

items.title: Why Darwin is a target for major crime syndicates looking to sell cheap tobacco
items.description: Convenience stores selling cheap, illegally packaged cigarettes have been popping up across Darwin and businesses are worried that organised crime and gang violence are next.

items.title: Kerr and Carpenter hit the ground running for Chelsea in Asian Cup return
items.description: Sam Kerr scores and sets up another goal with the help of Matildas teammate Ellie Carpenter as the Australians return to London to help Chelsea take down Aston Villa.
